Govt. returns to house for additional $89.8B, pushing 2026 spending past $1.7 trillion

Nov 19, 2026 News

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 39:42
Instaread

(Kaieteur News) – The government has returned to the National Assembly seeking an additional $89.8 billion in supplementary funding, pushing total 2026 national expenditure past the $1.7 trillion mark just four months after lawmakers approved a $54.889 billion top-up to the original $1.558 trillion budget.

Presented on Wednesday by Senior Minister in the Office of the President with Responsibility for Finance, Dr. Ashni Singh, Financial Supplementary Papers Number 2 and 3 of 2026 are heavily weighted toward major infrastructure works, the Gas-to-Energy project, and absorbing fuel spikes for the power sector.

Under Financial Paper 2, additional resources were sought for the Ministries of Agriculture and Education to cover contingency fund advances for the period July 31 to November 10, 2026. These are to offset the cost of emergency repairs to the Guyana School of Agriculture and provide additional resources to meet increased security charges for the Ministry of Education.

Senior Minister with responsibility for Finance, Dr. Ashni Singh.

Under Financial Paper 3, the largest allocation being sought is $27.4 billion for the Ministry of Public Works to support its expanded work programme. This includes the rehabilitation of public and main access roads, hinterland roads, the Linden-Mabura Road and Kurupukari Bridge projects, as well as sea and river defence works.

Speaking with reporters on the sidelines, Minister of Public Works Juan Edghill explained that the additional $27.4 billion being sought is critical to facilitate the accelerated implementation of infrastructure projects beyond what was originally anticipated in the 2026 budget.

He said favourable weather conditions, contractor performance and efficient management by engineers had allowed the ministry to complete some projects and undertake additional works. An example he gave is the US$190 million Linden-Mabura Hill Road, noting that while the government was completing the 121-kilometre stretch to Mabura Hill, it had already signed a contract for another 30 kilometres beyond that point.

The second-largest allocation being sought is $24.7 billion for the Gas-to-Energy (GTE) project under the Office of the Prime Minister.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Public Utilities and Aviation is seeking an additional $11.3 billion to provide resources for power entities in Linden, Mabaruma, Mahdia, Port Kaituma, Moruca and Matthew’s Ridge. Of that amount, $8 billion is allocated to the Guyana Power and Light Inc. (GPL), in keeping with the Government’s commitment to absorb elevated fuel costs associated with global developments, ensuring that these costs are not passed on to consumers through higher electricity tariffs.

It was outlined that since the war began at the end of February, oil prices climbed from about US$71 per barrel to a peak of more than US$144 per barrel in April, an increase of more than 104 per cent. As at the end of October, prices stood roughly 67 per cent above their pre-war level.

The Ministry of Public Utilities and Aviation is also seeking an additional $1.6 billion to support an expanded work programme at the Cheddi Jagan International Airport (CJIA).

As it relates to the Ministry of Agriculture, government is seeking $8.2 billion for the Guyana Sugar Corporation (GuySuCo) to cover increased operational cost and $2.7 billion to cover expanded work programme for the National Drainage and Irrigation Authority (NDIA).

Moreover, under the Ministry of Human Services and Social Security, government is seeking $10 billion in additional resources to provide for old age pension and public assistance beneficiaries.

The supplementary provision also includes $1 billion for additional resources to complete the distribution of the $100,000 cash grant to the remaining registrants who have yet to receive their payments.

In the health sector, government is seeking approval for an additional $809 million for the Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation (GPHC), in keeping with its commitment to improving health services.

Under the Ministry of Home Affairs, approval is being sought for an additional $34.7 million to support the expanded work programmes of the Guyana Police Force (GPF) and $411.8 million for the Guyana Prison Service (GFS).

Additionally, government is seeking $50.3 million under the Ministry of Labour and Manpower Planning to support the expanded work programme of the Board of Industrial Training (BIT).

Dr. Singh noted that the additional resources reflect the pace at which the Government is delivering on its commitment to improving the well-being of Guyanese and the need to ensure that projects are completed in a timely manner.

Just four months ago, the Committee of Supply approved $54.889 billion in supplementary funding for government, following approval of the $1.558 trillion budget for 2026.

That supplementary provision included an additional $19 billion for the GTE project, $4.5 billion for the Ministry of Agriculture to support the National Drainage and Irrigation Authority (NDIA), and $8.5 billion for the Ministry of Public Works.

The Ministry of Public Utilities and Aviation also received $496.3 million, specifically for coastal water supply and the maintenance of hinterland and coastal airstrips.

Additionally, $17.5 billion was approved for the Ministry of Housing to facilitate an expanded work programme, while the Ministry of Health received $337.9 million to facilitate the rental of buildings. The Ministry of Home Affairs also sought $60 million in additional resources for an accelerated work programme.
